-- | Name resolution: which surface spellings denote which declarations.
--   
--   Nothing in this module mentions a scope, a <a>Name</a>, or the kind
--   <tt>S</tt>, and that is the point. Resolution decides <i>which
--   declaration</i> an identifier denotes; the foil decides <i>which
--   index</i> a binder has. The first runs before the second and cannot
--   know its answers, so the two are separated here by a type parameter: a
--   <a>Table</a> maps a spelling to whatever the elaborator wants to hand
--   back, and this module never looks inside it.
--   
--   The practical consequence for this demo is that restricting what a
--   client can name (<tt>private</tt>, and what an <tt>import</tt> brings
--   in) is a computation on <a>Table</a> alone. It never touches a term,
--   so a private helper stays perfectly reducible while being unnameable.
--   That is the distinction between what can be <i>named</i> and what can
--   be <i>reduced</i>, and it is why narrowing needs no support from the
--   library at all.
--   
--   <h2>Influences</h2>
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>Separating resolution from everything downstream of it, and
--   treating a module as a construct that is named, encapsulates
--   declarations and can be imported rather than as a primitive, follows
--   Néron, Tolmach, Visser and Wachsmuth's <a>A Theory of Name
--   Resolution</a> (ESOP 2015). None of the scope-graph machinery is
--   reproduced here; the two-stage split is.</li>
--   <li><a>visibleAt</a> and <a>openNamespace</a> follow Lean 4's
--   <a>ResolveName</a> (<tt>resolveUsingNamespace</tt>,
--   <tt>resolveOpenDecls</tt>), with one simplification: Lean collects
--   every candidate and reports an ambiguity, whereas here a nearer
--   declaration silently shadows a farther one.</li>
--   <li>Restricting the resolver's table rather than the environment is
--   Jon Sterling's, from the <a>Pterodactyl worklog</a>, where
--   <tt>NarrowToUnit</tt> runs before <tt>ElaborateUnit</tt>.</li>
--   </ul>
module Language.MLTT.Resolve

-- | A namespace path, outermost segment first. The empty path is the top
--   level of a module.
--   
--   A path has nothing to do with the file a declaration lives in:
--   <tt>module Data.Nat</tt> may declare <tt>namespace Peano</tt>, and
--   importers then say <tt>Peano.zero</tt>. The module name orders the
--   build; the namespace qualifies the name.
type Path = [String]

-- | Split a dotted identifier into its segments.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; segments (Raw.VarIdent "Data.Nat.zero")
--   ["Data","Nat","zero"]
--   </pre>
segments :: VarIdent -> [String]

-- | Show a raw identifier as it was written.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; prettyVarIdent (Raw.VarIdent "Data.Nat.zero")
--   "Data.Nat.zero"
--   </pre>
prettyVarIdent :: VarIdent -> String

-- | Join segments back into an identifier.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; joinSegments ["Data","Nat","zero"]
--   VarIdent "Data.Nat.zero"
--   </pre>
joinSegments :: [String] -> VarIdent

-- | Qualify a name by a namespace path.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; qualify ["Data","Nat"] (Raw.VarIdent "zero")
--   VarIdent "Data.Nat.zero"
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; qualify [] (Raw.VarIdent "zero")
--   VarIdent "zero"
--   </pre>
qualify :: Path -> VarIdent -> VarIdent

-- | Every spelling nameable in some context, and what it denotes.
--   
--   The type of what it denotes is a parameter: the elaborator uses this
--   at <tt><a>Name</a> n</tt>, and the doctests here use it at
--   <a>String</a>.
type Table v = Map VarIdent v

-- | Which spellings a table of <i>fully qualified</i> names offers at a
--   given namespace path.
--   
--   A declaration <tt>A.B.f</tt> is nameable as <tt>f</tt> from inside
--   <tt>A.B</tt>, as <tt>B.f</tt> from inside <tt>A</tt>, and as
--   <tt>A.B.f</tt> from anywhere. The rule is one line: strip any prefix
--   of the current path. Longer prefixes are applied later and so win, so
--   a nearer declaration shadows a farther one of the same spelling.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Map.keys (visibleAt [] declared)
--   [VarIdent "Bool.true",VarIdent "Nat.Extra.double",VarIdent "Nat.zero"]
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Map.keys (visibleAt ["Nat"] declared)
--   [VarIdent "Bool.true",VarIdent "Extra.double",VarIdent "Nat.Extra.double",VarIdent "Nat.zero",VarIdent "zero"]
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Map.keys (visibleAt ["Nat","Extra"] declared)
--   [VarIdent "Bool.true",VarIdent "Extra.double",VarIdent "Nat.Extra.double",VarIdent "Nat.zero",VarIdent "double",VarIdent "zero"]
--   </pre>
visibleAt :: Path -> Table v -> Table v

-- | Bring the contents of a namespace into scope unqualified.
--   
--   Every spelling starting with the given prefix gains a second spelling
--   with that prefix stripped. The qualified spellings stay, so <tt>open
--   Nat</tt> never hides <tt>Nat.zero</tt>.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Map.keys (openNamespace (Raw.VarIdent "Nat") (visibleAt [] declared))
--   [VarIdent "Bool.true",VarIdent "Extra.double",VarIdent "Nat.Extra.double",VarIdent "Nat.zero",VarIdent "zero"]
--   </pre>
--   
--   Opening a namespace that does not exist brings in nothing, and is not
--   an error:
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Map.keys (openNamespace (Raw.VarIdent "Missing") declared) == Map.keys declared
--   True
--   </pre>
openNamespace :: VarIdent -> Table v -> Table v

-- | Whether a declaration leaves the module that declares it.
data Visibility

-- | Exported: an importing module may name it.
Public :: Visibility

-- | Not exported. An importing module cannot <i>name</i> it, and can still
--   <i>reduce</i> through it, since withholding a spelling touches no
--   term.
Private :: Visibility

-- | Add a declaration to what a module exports, if it is public.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Map.keys (export Public (Raw.VarIdent "Nat.two") "Nat.two" Map.empty)
--   [VarIdent "Nat.two"]
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; Map.keys (export Private (Raw.VarIdent "Nat.two") "Nat.two" Map.empty)
--   []
--   </pre>
export :: Visibility -> VarIdent -> v -> Table v -> Table v

-- | Spellings in scope that end in the same segment as an unresolved one.
--   
--   <tt>Nat.quadruple</tt> is a plausible thing to have meant by
--   <tt>quadruple</tt>, and in a language with namespaces it is usually
--   the only useful hint there is.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; suggestions (Raw.VarIdent "double") (Map.keys declared)
--   [VarIdent "Nat.Extra.double"]
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; suggestions (Raw.VarIdent "nope") (Map.keys declared)
--   []
--   </pre>
suggestions :: VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> [VarIdent]
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Language.MLTT.Resolve.Visibility
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Resolve.Visibility
instance GHC.Generics.Generic Language.MLTT.Resolve.Visibility
instance GHC.Read.Read Language.MLTT.Resolve.Visibility
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Resolve.Visibility


-- | The <a>FreeFoilConfig</a> driving the Template Haskell generation for
--   MLTT.
--   
--   There is a single term sort, so a single <a>FreeFoilTermConfig</a>.
--   Patterns are a proper syntactic category (<a>Pattern'</a>, with
--   wildcards, variables and pairs), which is what makes this demo
--   exercise free foil's <i>custom pattern</i> layer rather than a flat
--   list of binders.
module Language.MLTT.FreeFoilConfig

-- | Name a bound variable after its underlying raw name.
intToVarIdent :: RawName -> VarIdent

-- | The variable constructor, with the annotation erased.
rawVar :: VarIdent -> Term' a

-- | Wrap a raw term into a raw scoped term, with the annotation erased.
rawScopedTerm :: Term' a -> ScopedTerm' a

-- | Extract a raw term from a raw scoped term.
rawScopeToTerm :: ScopedTerm' a -> Term' a

-- | The configuration used by <a>Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated</a>.
mlttConfig :: FreeFoilConfig

module Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex
alex_tab_size :: Int

alex_check :: AlexAddr
alex_deflt :: AlexAddr
alex_accept :: Array Int (AlexAcc user)
alex_actions :: Array Int (Posn -> String -> Token)
alex_action_3 :: Posn -> String -> Token
alex_action_4 :: Posn -> String -> Token
alex_action_5 :: Posn -> String -> Token
data AlexAddr
AlexA# :: Addr# -> AlexAddr
alexIndexInt16OffAddr :: AlexAddr -> Int# -> Int#
alexIndexInt32OffAddr :: AlexAddr -> Int# -> Int#
quickIndex :: Array Int (AlexAcc (Any :: Type)) -> Int -> AlexAcc (Any :: Type)
data AlexReturn a
AlexEOF :: AlexReturn a
AlexError :: !AlexInput -> AlexReturn a
AlexSkip :: !AlexInput -> !Int -> AlexReturn a
AlexToken :: !AlexInput -> !Int -> a -> AlexReturn a
alexScan :: (Posn, Char, [Byte], String) -> Int -> AlexReturn (Posn -> String -> Token)
alexScanUser :: t -> (Posn, Char, [Byte], String) -> Int -> AlexReturn (Posn -> String -> Token)
alex_scan_tkn :: t1 -> t2 -> Int# -> AlexInput -> Int# -> AlexLastAcc -> (AlexLastAcc, AlexInput)
data AlexLastAcc
AlexNone :: AlexLastAcc
AlexLastAcc :: !Int -> !AlexInput -> !Int -> AlexLastAcc
AlexLastSkip :: !AlexInput -> !Int -> AlexLastAcc
data AlexAcc user
AlexAccNone :: AlexAcc user
AlexAcc :: Int -> AlexAcc user
AlexAccSkip :: AlexAcc user

-- | Create a token with position.
tok :: (String -> Tok) -> Posn -> String -> Token

-- | Token without position.
data Tok

-- | Reserved word or symbol.
TK :: {-# UNPACK #-} !TokSymbol -> Tok

-- | String literal.
TL :: !String -> Tok

-- | Integer literal.
TI :: !String -> Tok

-- | Identifier.
TV :: !String -> Tok

-- | Float literal.
TD :: !String -> Tok

-- | Character literal.
TC :: !String -> Tok
T_VarIdent :: !String -> Tok

-- | Smart constructor for <a>Tok</a> for the sake of backwards
--   compatibility.
pattern TS :: String -> Int -> Tok

-- | Keyword or symbol tokens have a unique ID.
data TokSymbol
TokSymbol :: String -> !Int -> TokSymbol

-- | Keyword or symbol text.
[tsText] :: TokSymbol -> String

-- | Unique ID.
[tsID] :: TokSymbol -> !Int

-- | Token with position.
data Token
PT :: Posn -> Tok -> Token
Err :: Posn -> Token

-- | Pretty print a position.
printPosn :: Posn -> String

-- | Pretty print the position of the first token in the list.
tokenPos :: [Token] -> String

-- | Get the position of a token.
tokenPosn :: Token -> Posn

-- | Get line and column of a token.
tokenLineCol :: Token -> (Int, Int)

-- | Get line and column of a position.
posLineCol :: Posn -> (Int, Int)

-- | Convert a token into "position token" form.
mkPosToken :: Token -> ((Int, Int), String)

-- | Convert a token to its text.
tokenText :: Token -> String

-- | Convert a token to a string.
prToken :: Token -> String

-- | Finite map from text to token organized as binary search tree.
data BTree

-- | Nil (leaf).
N :: BTree

-- | Binary node.
B :: String -> Tok -> BTree -> BTree -> BTree

-- | Convert potential keyword into token or use fallback conversion.
eitherResIdent :: (String -> Tok) -> String -> Tok

-- | The keywords and symbols of the language organized as binary search
--   tree.
resWords :: BTree

-- | Unquote string literal.
unescapeInitTail :: String -> String
data Posn
Pn :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> Posn
alexStartPos :: Posn
alexMove :: Posn -> Char -> Posn
type Byte = Word8
type AlexInput = (Posn, Char, [Byte], String)
tokens :: String -> [Token]
alexGetByte :: AlexInput -> Maybe (Byte, AlexInput)
alexInputPrevChar :: AlexInput -> Char

-- | Encode a Haskell String to a list of Word8 values, in UTF8 format.
utf8Encode :: Char -> [Word8]
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex.Posn
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex.Tok
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex.TokSymbol
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex.Token
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex.Posn
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex.Tok
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.MLTT.Syntax.Lex.TokSymbol

module Language.MLTT.Syntax.Layout
data LayoutDelimiters
LayoutDelimiters :: TokSymbol -> Maybe TokSymbol -> Maybe TokSymbol -> LayoutDelimiters
[delimSep] :: LayoutDelimiters -> TokSymbol

-- | Nothing for toplevel layout.
[delimOpen] :: LayoutDelimiters -> Maybe TokSymbol

-- | Nothing for toplevel layout.
[delimClose] :: LayoutDelimiters -> Maybe TokSymbol
layoutWords :: [(TokSymbol, LayoutDelimiters)]
layoutStopWords :: [TokSymbol]
layoutOpen :: [TokSymbol]
layoutClose :: [TokSymbol]
layoutSep :: [TokSymbol]
parenOpen :: [TokSymbol]
parenClose :: [TokSymbol]

-- | Report an error during layout resolution.
layoutError :: [Token] -> String -> a

-- | Replace layout syntax with explicit layout tokens.
resolveLayout :: Bool -> [Token] -> [Token]
type Position = Posn
type Line = Int
type Column = Int

-- | Entry of the layout stack.
data Block

-- | An implicit layout block with its start column.
Implicit :: LayoutDelimiters -> Status -> Column -> Block
Explicit :: Block

-- | Get current indentation. 0 if we are in an explicit block.
indentation :: Block -> Column

-- | Check if s block is implicit.
isImplicit :: Block -> Bool
data Status

-- | A layout column that has not been confirmed by a line break
Tentative :: Status

-- | A layout column that has been confirmed by a line break.
Definitive :: Status

-- | Add a new implicit layout block.
addImplicit :: LayoutDelimiters -> Position -> Position -> [Block] -> [Block]

-- | Confirm tentative blocks that are not more indented than <tt>col</tt>.
confirm :: Column -> [Block] -> [Block]

-- | Get the position immediately to the right of the given token. If no
--   token is given, gets the first position in the file.
afterPrev :: Maybe Token -> Position

-- | Get the position immediately to the right of the given token.
nextPos :: Token -> Position

-- | Get the number of characters in the token.
tokenLength :: Token -> Int

-- | Create a position symbol token.
sToken :: Position -> TokSymbol -> Token

-- | Get the line number of a token.
line :: Token -> Line

-- | Get the column number of a token.
column :: Token -> Column

-- | Is the following token on a new line?
newLine :: Maybe Token -> Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a word is a layout start token.
isLayout :: Token -> Maybe LayoutDelimiters

-- | Check if a token is one of the given symbols.
isTokenIn :: [TokSymbol] -> Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is a layout stop token.
isStop :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is the layout open token.
isLayoutOpen :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is the layout separator token.
isLayoutSep :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is the layout close token.
isLayoutClose :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is an opening parenthesis.
isParenOpen :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is a closing parenthesis.
isParenClose :: Token -> Bool
