-- | Everything about MLTT that is <i>generated</i> rather than written.
--   
--   The scope-safe term type, the signature bifunctor, the pattern
--   synonyms and the conversions to and from the raw (BNFC) syntax all
--   come out of <a>mkFreeFoil</a> and <a>mkFreeFoilConversions</a>. What
--   is written by hand here is only the instances that the generated types
--   need and Template Haskell cannot supply: the <a>GenericK</a>
--   representations, the bifunctor instances of the signature, and the
--   pattern instances of <a>Pattern'</a>.
module Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. A scoped (and scope-safe)
--   version of <a>Term'</a>.
type ScopedTerm' a = ScopedAST Pattern' a Term'Sig a

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. A scope-safe version of
--   <a>Term'</a>.
type Term' a = AST Pattern' a Term'Sig a

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. A signature based on
--   <a>Term'</a>.
data Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Pi</a>.
[PiSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> scope -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Sigma</a>.
[SigmaSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> scope -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Lam</a>.
[LamSig] :: forall a scope term. a -> scope -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Let</a>.
[LetSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> scope -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Arrow</a>.
[ArrowSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Product</a>.
[ProductSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>App</a>.
[AppSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>First</a>.
[FirstSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Second</a>.
[SecondSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Universe</a>.
[UniverseSig] :: forall a scope term. a -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>UnitType</a>.
[UnitTypeSig] :: forall a scope term. a -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>UnitVal</a>.
[UnitValSig] :: forall a scope term. a -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>IdType</a>.
[IdTypeSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> term -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Refl</a>.
[ReflSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>J</a>.
[JSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> term -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Pair</a>.
[PairSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | Corresponds to <a>Ann</a>.
[AnnSig] :: forall a term scope. a -> term -> term -> Term'Sig a scope term

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. A binding type, scope-safe
--   version of <a>Pattern'</a>.
data Pattern' a (o :: S) (i :: S)

-- | Corresponds to <a>PatternWildcard</a>.
[PatternWildcard] :: forall a (o :: S). a -> Pattern' a o o

-- | Corresponds to <a>PatternVar</a>.
[PatternVar] :: forall a (o :: S) (i :: S). a -> NameBinder o i -> Pattern' a o i

-- | Corresponds to <a>PatternPair</a>.
[PatternPair] :: forall a (o :: S) (i1 :: S) (i :: S). a -> Pattern' a o i1 -> Pattern' a i1 i -> Pattern' a o i

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Ann</a>.
pattern Ann :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Pair</a>.
pattern Pair :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>J</a>.
pattern J :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Refl</a>.
pattern Refl :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>IdType</a>.
pattern IdType :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>UnitVal</a>.
pattern UnitVal :: a -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>UnitType</a>.
pattern UnitType :: a -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Universe</a>.
pattern Universe :: a -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Second</a>.
pattern Second :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>First</a>.
pattern First :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>App</a>.
pattern App :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Product</a>.
pattern Product :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Arrow</a>.
pattern Arrow :: a -> Term' a o -> Term' a o -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Let</a>.
pattern Let :: () => a -> Term' a o -> Pattern' a o i -> Term' a i -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Lam</a>.
pattern Lam :: () => a -> Pattern' a o i -> Term' a i -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Sigma</a>.
pattern Sigma :: () => a -> Term' a o -> Pattern' a o i -> Term' a i -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Pattern synonym for an
--   <a>AST</a> node of type <a>Pi</a>.
pattern Pi :: () => a -> Term' a o -> Pattern' a o i -> Term' a i -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. A helper used to convert from
--   scope-safe to raw representation.
fromTerm'Sig :: Term'Sig a (Pattern' a, ScopedTerm' a) (Term' a) -> Term' a

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Convert a scope-safe to a raw
--   binding, naming the binders from their indices with the given
--   function. The same function must name the bound-variable references,
--   or a reference comes out free of its own binder.
fromPattern'With :: forall a (o :: S) (i :: S). (Int -> VarIdent) -> Pattern' a o i -> Pattern' a

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Convert a scope-safe to a raw
--   binding, with the display naming.
fromPattern' :: forall a (o :: S) (i :: S). Pattern' a o i -> Pattern' a

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Convert from scope-safe to
--   raw representation.
fromTerm' :: forall a (o :: S). Term' a o -> Term' a

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. A helper used to convert from
--   raw to scope-safe representation.
toTerm'Sig :: Term' a -> Either VarIdent (Term'Sig a (Pattern' a, ScopedTerm' a) (Term' a))

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Convert from raw to
--   scope-safe binding (CPS-style), allocating the binders within a given
--   range; see <a>withFreshIn</a>.
toPattern'In :: forall (o :: S) a r. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => NameRange -> Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Pattern' a -> (forall (i :: S). DExt o i => Pattern' a o i -> Map VarIdent (Name i) -> r) -> r

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Convert from raw to
--   scope-safe binding (CPS-style). This is <a>toPattern'In</a> at
--   <a>fullNameRange</a>.
toPattern' :: forall (o :: S) a r. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Pattern' a -> (forall (i :: S). DExt o i => Pattern' a o i -> Map VarIdent (Name i) -> r) -> r

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Convert from raw to
--   scope-safe representation, calling <a>error</a> on an identifier that
--   does not resolve. See <a>tryToTerm'</a>.
toTerm' :: forall (o :: S) a. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Term' a -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Convert from raw to
--   scope-safe representation, reporting the first identifier that does
--   not resolve.
tryToTerm' :: forall (o :: S) a. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Term' a -> Either (UnresolvedName VarIdent) (Term' a o)

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Same as <a>tryToTerm'</a>,
--   except that some identifiers may resolve to a whole term rather than
--   to a variable.
tryToTerm'With :: forall (o :: S) a. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Map VarIdent (Term' a o) -> Term' a -> Either (UnresolvedName VarIdent) (Term' a o)

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Same as <a>toTerm'</a>,
--   except that the binders introduced by the conversion are allocated
--   within the given range; see <a>withFreshIn</a>.
toTerm'In :: forall (o :: S) a. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => NameRange -> Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Term' a -> Term' a o

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Same as <a>tryToTerm'</a>,
--   except that the binders introduced by the conversion are allocated
--   within the given range; see <a>withFreshIn</a>.
tryToTerm'In :: forall (o :: S) a. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => NameRange -> Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Term' a -> Either (UnresolvedName VarIdent) (Term' a o)

-- | <i>Generated</i> with <a>mkFreeFoil</a>. Same as
--   <a>tryToTerm'With</a>, except that the binders introduced by the
--   conversion are allocated within the given range; see
--   <a>withFreshIn</a>.
tryToTerm'WithIn :: forall (o :: S) a. (Distinct o, Ord VarIdent) => NameRange -> Scope o -> Map VarIdent (Name o) -> Map VarIdent (Term' a o) -> Term' a -> Either (UnresolvedName VarIdent) (Term' a o)

-- | Source text as the parser receives it: the contents of a file, of
--   standard input, or of one interactive step. The <a>IsString</a>
--   instance lets tests and doctests write literals.
newtype SourceText
SourceText :: String -> SourceText
[sourceText] :: SourceText -> String

-- | Assemble a source from its lines, <a>unlines</a>-style.
sourceLines :: [String] -> SourceText

-- | What the parser reports when the input is not MLTT.
type ParseError = String

-- | Parse a raw term, calling <a>error</a> if it does not parse.
unsafeParse :: ([Token] -> Either ParseError a) -> SourceText -> a

-- | Parse a raw program: a sequence of modules, laid out.
parseProgram :: SourceText -> Either ParseError Program

-- | Parse a run of declarations, laid out as a module body is: what one
--   interactive input holds.
parseDecls :: SourceText -> Either ParseError [Decl]

-- | Parse a run of imports, laid out as a module header is: what an
--   interactive <tt>import</tt> line holds.
parseImports :: SourceText -> Either ParseError [Import]

-- | Convert back to raw syntax, naming free and bound variables
--   separately.
--   
--   A variable free in the whole term is named from a <a>NameMap</a>; a
--   bound one is named from its index. Keeping the two apart matters
--   because raw names are not unique across scope indices: a definition's
--   body is elaborated before the definition's own name is allocated, so
--   <tt>def f := λ x ⇒ x</tt> gives both <tt>f</tt> and the <tt>x</tt> it
--   binds the raw name 0.
fromTermWith :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => (Int -> VarIdent) -> NameMap n VarIdent -> Term' a n -> Term' a

-- | Print a term, naming free and bound variables separately.
showTermWith :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => (Int -> VarIdent) -> NameMap n VarIdent -> Term' a n -> String

-- | <a>fromTermWith</a>, with one naming function covering both the binder
--   occurrences (through the generated <a>fromPattern'With</a>) and the
--   bound-variable references.
fromTermNamed :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => (Int -> VarIdent) -> NameMap n VarIdent -> Term' a n -> Term' a

-- | Print a term with one naming function for everything bound.
showTermNamed :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => (Int -> VarIdent) -> NameMap n VarIdent -> Term' a n -> String

-- | A scope-safe MLTT term, annotated with a source position.
type Term = Term' BNFC'Position

-- | A scope-safe MLTT pattern, annotated with a source position.
type Pattern = Pattern' BNFC'Position

-- | A scope-safe MLTT term under a binder, annotated with a source
--   position.
type ScopedTerm = ScopedTerm' BNFC'Position
instance Data.Bifoldable.Bifoldable (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a)
instance Data.Bifunctor.Bifunctor (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a)
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary p1 => Data.Binary.Class.Binary (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' p1 n l)
instance (Data.Binary.Class.Binary a, Data.Binary.Class.Binary s, Data.Binary.Class.Binary t) => Data.Binary.Class.Binary (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a s t)
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Language.MLTT.Syntax.Abs.VarIdent
instance Data.Bitraversable.Bitraversable (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a)
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.CoSinkable (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' a)
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.SourceText
instance Data.Foldable.Foldable (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a scope)
instance GHC.Base.Functor (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a scope)
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' a o)
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' a)
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern'
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a scope)
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a)
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' a o i)
instance Generics.Kind.GenericK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a scope term)
instance GHC.Generics.Generic (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a scope term)
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.HasNameBinders (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' a)
instance Data.String.IsString (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term' Language.MLTT.Syntax.Abs.BNFC'Position 'Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.VoidS)
instance Data.String.IsString Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.SourceText
instance GHC.Base.Monoid Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.SourceText
instance GHC.Base.Semigroup Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.SourceText
instance GHC.Show.Show (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term' a n)
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.SourceText
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.SinkableK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' a)
instance Data.Traversable.Traversable (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a scope)
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.UnifiableInPattern Language.MLTT.Syntax.Abs.BNFC'Position
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.UnifiablePattern (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Pattern' a)
instance Data.ZipMatchK.Generic.ZipMatchK a => Data.ZipMatchK.Generic.ZipMatchK (Language.MLTT.Impl.Generated.Term'Sig a)
instance Data.ZipMatchK.Generic.ZipMatchK Language.MLTT.Syntax.Abs.BNFC'Position


-- | Evaluation and conversion for MLTT.
--   
--   Reduction is deliberately naive: weak head normal forms computed by
--   <a>whnf</a>, full normal forms by <a>nf</a>, and conversion by
--   &lt;math&gt;-equivalence of normal forms (<a>conv</a>). The library
--   supplies substitution and &lt;math&gt;-equivalence, so what is written
--   here is only the reduction rules themselves.
module Language.MLTT.Eval

-- | Replace the non-dependent <tt>A → B</tt> and <tt>A × B</tt> by <tt>Π
--   (_ : A) → B</tt> and <tt>Σ (_ : A) × B</tt>.
--   
--   Both are genuinely sugar: a wildcard pattern binds nothing, so the
--   codomain cannot depend on the domain. Doing this once, right after
--   parsing, keeps the evaluator and the type checker down to one rule per
--   former.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; desugar ("𝟙 → 𝟙" :: Term Foil.VoidS)
--   Π (_ : 𝟙) → 𝟙
--   </pre>
desugar :: forall a (n :: S). Term' a n -> Term' a n

-- | The substitution that matches a pattern against a term.
--   
--   Each variable the pattern binds is sent to the corresponding
--   projection of the term, so that a pair pattern is eliminated by
--   <tt>π₁</tt> and <tt>π₂</tt> rather than by a separate matching
--   judgement. This is the one place where the shape of a custom pattern
--   matters to the semantics.
matchPattern :: forall a (n :: S) (l :: S) (o :: S). DExt n o => Pattern' a n l -> Term' a o -> Substitution (Term' a) l o

-- | Instantiate the body of a binder: substitute a term for the pattern it
--   was bound by. This is the workhorse of &lt;math&gt;, of <tt>let</tt>,
--   and of every rule in the type checker that has to look underneath a
--   binder.
--   
--   The target scope <tt>o</tt> may be larger than the pattern's own scope
--   <tt>n</tt>, which is what lets the type checker open a &lt;math&gt;
--   and the &lt;math&gt;-type it is checked against at one and the same
--   fresh variable.
instantiate :: forall (n :: S) (o :: S) a (l :: S). DExt n o => Scope o -> Pattern' a n l -> Term' a o -> Term' a l -> Term' a o

-- | What a name in scope may unfold to: <a>Nothing</a> for a local
--   variable, <a>Just</a> for a top-level definition that
--   &lt;math&gt;-reduction unfolds.
--   
--   This is a <tt>newtype</tt> rather than a bare <a>Maybe</a> so that it
--   is <a>Sinkable</a>, which is what lets <a>extendDefs</a> enter a
--   binder in &lt;math&gt;.
newtype Def a (n :: S)
Def :: Maybe (Term' a n) -> Def a (n :: S)
[getDef] :: Def a (n :: S) -> Maybe (Term' a n)

-- | A <i>total</i> map from the names in scope to what they unfold to.
type Defs a (n :: S) = NameMap n Def a n

-- | No definitions in the empty scope.
emptyDefs :: Defs a 'VoidS

-- | Enter a pattern: every name it binds is a local variable, so unfolds
--   to nothing.
extendDefs :: forall binder (n :: S) (l :: S) a. (CoSinkable binder, DExt n l) => binder n l -> Defs a n -> Defs a l

-- | Compute the weak head normal form of a term.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; let scope = Foil.emptyScope
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; whnf scope emptyDefs (desugar ("(λ (x, y) ⇒ y) (tt, λ z ⇒ z)" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   λ x0 ⇒ x0
--   </pre>
--   
--   Projections reduce on an explicit pair, and <tt>J</tt> on
--   <tt>refl</tt>:
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; whnf scope emptyDefs (desugar ("π₁ (tt, 𝕌)" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   tt
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; whnf scope emptyDefs (desugar ("J (λ x ⇒ λ p ⇒ 𝟙, tt, refl (tt))" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   tt
--   </pre>
whnf :: forall a (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Defs a n -> Term' a n -> Term' a n

-- | Compute the full normal form of a term, reducing under binders.
--   
--   Note that MLTT here has type-in-type, so this can diverge on a
--   well-typed term. That is a deliberate simplification: the demo is
--   about scoping, not about consistency.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; nf Foil.emptyScope emptyDefs (desugar ("λ f ⇒ λ x ⇒ (λ y ⇒ f y) x" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   λ x0 ⇒ x0
--   </pre>
nf :: forall a (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Defs a n -> Term' a n -> Term' a n

-- | η-reduce a λ that does nothing but apply a term to the variable it
--   binds.
--   
--   <tt>λ x ⇒ f x</tt> is <tt>f</tt>, provided <tt>f</tt> does not use
--   <tt>x</tt> itself. That proviso is exactly what free-foil's
--   <i>restriction</i> answers: <a>unsinkAST</a> succeeds when the
--   function part of the body lives in the scope outside the binder, so
--   the test is a subset check on the support and a term that passes is
--   not rebuilt.
--   
--   This is η as a reduction rather than as an expansion, which is why it
--   can sit in <a>nf</a>: contracting needs no types, whereas expanding
--   would need to know that the term is of a function type, and the
--   evaluator here is untyped.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; nf Foil.emptyScope emptyDefs (desugar ("λ f ⇒ λ x ⇒ f x" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   λ x0 ⇒ x0
--   </pre>
--   
--   The function part has to be free of the binder. Here it is not, so
--   nothing happens:
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; nf Foil.emptyScope emptyDefs (desugar ("λ x ⇒ x x" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   λ x0 ⇒ x0 x0
--   </pre>
--   
--   Only a λ binding a single variable qualifies. A pair pattern would be
--   surjective pairing, which is a different rule and not implemented.
etaReduce :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Scope n -> Term' a n -> Term' a n

-- | Conversion: are two terms equal up to reduction and renaming of bound
--   variables?
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; conv Foil.emptyScope emptyDefs (desugar ("(λ x ⇒ x) tt" :: Term Foil.VoidS)) (desugar "tt")
--   True
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; conv Foil.emptyScope emptyDefs (desugar ("λ x ⇒ x" :: Term Foil.VoidS)) (desugar "λ y ⇒ tt")
--   False
--   </pre>
conv :: forall (n :: S) a. (Distinct n, ZipMatchK a) => Scope n -> Defs a n -> Term' a n -> Term' a n -> Bool
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.Sinkable (Language.MLTT.Eval.Def a)


-- | Module parameters as a labelled telescope, and closing a declaration
--   over the parameters it uses.
--   
--   The telescope itself (the type, its pattern instances, and the
--   dependency closure) lives in the library, in
--   <a>Control.Monad.Foil.Telescope</a>. What stays in the demo is the
--   instantiation: labels are spellings, payloads are types, and
--   <a>discharge</a> folds the closed type into <tt>Π</tt>s and the value
--   into <tt>λ</tt>s.
--   
--   A parametrised module
--   
--   <pre>
--   module Group (A : 𝕌) (m : A → A → A) ;
--   def twice : A → A := λ x ⇒ m x x
--   </pre>
--   
--   checks every declaration with its parameters in scope, and then closes
--   each one over exactly the parameters that declaration turns out to
--   use, so that what leaves the module is an ordinary closed definition
--   <tt>Group.twice : Π (A : 𝕌) → Π (m : A → A → A) → A → A</tt>. A
--   declaration that uses no parameter is closed over nothing and stays a
--   plain constant. An optional <tt>over (…)</tt> clause states that set
--   in the source, and is checked against the computed one by
--   <a>checkDischarge</a>.
--   
--   <h2>Where the scope restriction is</h2>
--   
--   This is the place the demo needs free-foil's scope <i>restriction</i>
--   rather than its extension. Checking happens in the scope <tt>p</tt>
--   that the parameters extend the module's scope <tt>n</tt> to; the
--   result has to come back to <tt>n</tt>, because <tt>n</tt> is where the
--   module's exports live and where the next module starts.
--   
--   It is done in three steps, and the point of the arrangement is that
--   the term is walked a fixed number of times rather than once per
--   parameter:
--   
--   <ol>
--   <li><a>supportOf</a> the type and the value, once each.</li>
--   <li><a>closeOverTelescope</a> closes that set under the parameter
--   types. Keeping <tt>(x : A)</tt> puts <tt>A</tt> into the result, so
--   <tt>A</tt> has to be kept as well. One pass from the inside out is
--   enough, since a parameter's type mentions only the parameters before
--   it.</li>
--   <li><a>withThinnedNameBinderList</a> cuts the chain of binders down to
--   that set in one step, and <a>discharge</a> rebuilds the abstractions
--   along the thinned chain, restricting each parameter type and the body
--   into it.</li>
--   </ol>
--   
--   The alternative, asking <a>unsinkAST</a> at every parameter whether
--   the term can do without it, is shorter to write and walks the whole
--   term once per parameter.
module Language.MLTT.Telescope

-- | A module's parameters: the labels are spellings, the payloads are
--   types.
type ParamTelescope a = Telescope VarIdent Term' a

-- | A declaration after being closed over the module's parameters.
data Discharged a (n :: S)
Discharged :: Term' a n -> Term' a n -> [VarIdent] -> Discharged a (n :: S)

-- | The type, wrapped in a <tt>Π</tt> for each parameter kept.
[dischargedType] :: Discharged a (n :: S) -> Term' a n

-- | The value, wrapped in a <tt>λ</tt> for each parameter kept.
[dischargedValue] :: Discharged a (n :: S) -> Term' a n

-- | Which parameters those were, outermost first.
[dischargedOver] :: Discharged a (n :: S) -> [VarIdent]

-- | Close a checked declaration over a given set of the module's
--   parameters.
--   
--   The type and the value are closed over together, over the same
--   parameters, since <tt>f : T</tt> and <tt>f := v</tt> have to stay a
--   matching pair: if only the value mentions a parameter, the type still
--   gains a (non-dependent) <tt>Π</tt> for it.
--   
--   Given <a>Nothing</a>, the set is the computed one and the result is a
--   <a>Right</a>. Given a <i>declared</i> set, <a>Left</a> names the
--   parameters the declaration needs and that set does not have, which is
--   the useful thing to say about a wrong <tt>over</tt> clause.
discharge :: forall a (n :: S) (l :: S). (Distinct n, Distinct l) => a -> Scope n -> ParamTelescope a n l -> Maybe (NameSet l) -> Term' a l -> Term' a l -> Either [VarIdent] (Discharged a n)

-- | Check a declared <tt>over</tt> clause against the parameters actually
--   kept.
--   
--   The clause is optional, and it never changes what is defined: the
--   computed list is authoritative either way, so an accepted clause is
--   one that agrees with it. Both directions are reported, since listing a
--   parameter that is not used is as much a mistake in the documentation
--   as omitting one that is.
--   
--   It is spelled <tt>over</tt> rather than <tt>uses</tt> because rzk has
--   a <tt>uses</tt> clause that is a different thing: mandatory, and
--   listing the implicit assumptions of a definition rather than the
--   parameters of its module.
checkDischarge :: Discharge -> [VarIdent] -> Either String ()


-- | A bidirectional type checker for MLTT.
--   
--   The interesting part is not the typing rules, which are standard, but
--   how little scope handling they need: the foil's <a>withFresh</a>
--   allocates the variable, <a>NameMap</a> holds the context, and
--   <a>instantiate</a> opens a binder. Nothing here manipulates a de
--   Bruijn index or a name supply by hand.
--   
--   One rule is worth reading for the design: to check <tt>λ p ⇒ e</tt>
--   against <tt>Π (q : A) → B</tt>, <a>check</a> allocates <i>one</i>
--   fresh variable and opens both <tt>p</tt> and <tt>q</tt> at it. The two
--   patterns need not have the same shape, and neither needs to bind
--   anything, so <tt>λ (x, y) ⇒ e</tt> against <tt>Π (z : Σ …) → B</tt>
--   and <tt>λ _ ⇒ e</tt> against <tt>Π (z : A) → B</tt> are both handled
--   by the same rule.
--   
--   <h2>What this checker deliberately does not do</h2>
--   
--   It is a demonstration of scope handling, not a type checker anyone
--   should copy wholesale. Four omissions are worth naming, because each
--   is somebody else's work in this ecosystem rather than a gap to be
--   filled here.
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><b>No elaboration.</b> <a>infer</a> returns a type and discards
--   everything else, so there is no elaborated output term, no implicit
--   arguments, and no inserted coercions. The library does have a
--   scope-indexed annotation layer
--   (<a>Control.Monad.Free.Foil.Annotated</a>); it is not used here.</li>
--   <li><b>No normalisation by evaluation.</b> Conversion normalises both
--   sides and compares them (<a>conv</a>). There are no closures, no
--   delayed substitutions, and no readback.</li>
--   <li><b>No generic typing algebra.</b> The rules below are written by
--   hand for this one signature. Deriving a checker from per-constructor
--   typing rules, and the Pfenning recipe that chooses the judgement, are
--   a separate line of work.</li>
--   <li><b>No metavariables.</b> No holes, no unification, no higher-order
--   matching. Generic second-order matching, higher-order preunification,
--   and pattern unification over free foil are Kudasov, Starikov, Ivanov,
--   and Afliatonov's, UNIF 2025 (<a>HAL record</a>), implemented in
--   <a>free-foil-hou</a>.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   It is also inconsistent on purpose: see <a>nf</a>.
module Language.MLTT.Typecheck

-- | Everything the type checker knows about the names in scope <tt>n</tt>:
--   the scope itself, a <i>total</i> map giving each name its type, and a
--   <i>total</i> map saying what each name unfolds to.
data Ctx a (n :: S)
Ctx :: Scope n -> NameMap n (Term' a n) -> Defs a n -> Ctx a (n :: S)
[ctxScope] :: Ctx a (n :: S) -> Scope n
[ctxTypes] :: Ctx a (n :: S) -> NameMap n (Term' a n)
[ctxDefs] :: Ctx a (n :: S) -> Defs a n

-- | The empty context.
emptyCtx :: Ctx a 'VoidS

-- | Extend a context with a fresh variable of a given type.
withVar :: forall (n :: S) a r. Distinct n => Ctx a n -> Term' a n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => Ctx a l -> Name l -> r) -> r

-- | Extend a context with a fresh variable, handing back its
--   <i>binder</i>.
--   
--   A caller that intends to abstract over the variable again later needs
--   the binder and not just the name, since a binder is what a <tt>Π</tt>
--   or a <tt>λ</tt> is built from. See <a>Language.MLTT.Telescope</a>.
withVarBinder :: forall (n :: S) a r. Distinct n => NameRange -> Ctx a n -> Term' a n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => Ctx a l -> NameBinder n l -> r) -> r

-- | Add one binder to a context. Sinking the two maps is &lt;math&gt;;
--   only the new entry is inserted.
--   
--   A top-level definition goes through this too, with a <a>Just</a>
--   value: it is an ordinary name in scope whose <a>Def</a> is not
--   <a>Nothing</a>, so &lt;math&gt;-reduction unfolds it and nothing else
--   has to change. That makes a top-level constant a <a>Name</a> in a
--   growing scope, which is one of the two possible designs for a global
--   environment.
extend :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) a. DExt n l => Ctx a n -> NameBinder n l -> Term' a n -> Maybe (Term' a n) -> Ctx a l

-- | Reduce a term to weak head normal form in a context.
whnfIn :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Ctx a n -> Term' a n -> Term' a n

-- | What the type checker reports. Terms are shown in the raw syntax, so
--   an error message reads like the source it came from.
type TypeError = String

-- | Infer the type of a term.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; infer emptyCtx (desugar ("(λ x ⇒ x : 𝟙 → 𝟙) tt" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   Right 𝟙
--   </pre>
--   
--   The second component of a pair is typed by substituting the first into
--   the Σ-type's codomain, so a projection is dependent even when the pair
--   is not:
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; infer emptyCtx (desugar ("π₂ (𝟙, tt)" :: Term Foil.VoidS))
--   Right 𝟙
--   </pre>
infer :: forall a (n :: S). (Distinct n, ZipMatchK a) => Ctx a n -> Term' a n -> Either TypeError (Term' a n)

-- | The type of the motive of <tt>J</tt>: <tt>Π (x : A) → Id(A, a, x) →
--   𝕌</tt>.
motiveType :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Scope n -> a -> Term' a n -> Term' a n -> Term' a n

-- | Check a term against a type.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; check emptyCtx (desugar ("λ A ⇒ λ x ⇒ x" :: Term Foil.VoidS)) (desugar "Π (A : 𝕌) → Π (x : A) → A")
--   Right ()
--   </pre>
--   
--   Pattern binders are checked against the type of what they destructure:
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; check emptyCtx (desugar ("λ (A, x) ⇒ x" :: Term Foil.VoidS)) (desugar "Π (p : Σ (A : 𝕌) × A) → π₁ p")
--   Right ()
--   </pre>
check :: forall a (n :: S). (Distinct n, ZipMatchK a) => Ctx a n -> Term' a n -> Term' a n -> Either TypeError ()

-- | A uniform "expected X, got Y" message.
expected :: forall a (n :: S). String -> Term' a n -> Term' a n -> TypeError


-- | The MLTT interpreter: the generated syntax, the evaluator, the type
--   checker and the resolver glued into a program that reads modules.
--   
--   A module is introduced by a <tt>module</tt> header and runs to the
--   next one. Usually a file holds one, and the interpreter takes any
--   number of files; but nothing stops a file from holding several, which
--   is what the tests and <tt>examples/modules.mltt</tt> do so that a
--   whole example fits in one place. Build order is computed over every
--   module the interpreter was given, wherever it came from.
--   
--   <pre>
--   module Data.Nat
--   import Prelude
--   
--   namespace Nat where
--     def id : Π (A : 𝕌) → A → A := λ A ⇒ λ x ⇒ x
--     private def helper : 𝟙 := tt
--   
--   open Nat
--   compute id 𝟙 tt
--   </pre>
--   
--   Everything lives in one growing foil scope: a top-level definition is
--   an ordinary <a>Name</a> whose <a>Def</a> says what it unfolds to, and
--   a module, namespace or <tt>import</tt> decides only <i>which spellings
--   can reach which name</i>. That split is what makes <tt>private</tt>
--   cheap, and it is worth stating plainly:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><a>envDeclared</a> is a name table, so making a helper private
--   removes a spelling and nothing else;</li>
--   <li><a>ctxDefs</a> is untouched by any of it, so conversion still
--   unfolds that helper wherever it already occurs in a checked term.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   A client therefore cannot <i>name</i> a private helper but can still
--   <i>reduce</i> through it, which is the behaviour a proof assistant
--   needs and the reason narrowing belongs above the library rather than
--   inside it.
module Language.MLTT.Impl

-- | What each name in scope is called: the read-back direction of a
--   <a>Table</a>.
--   
--   This is a <a>NameMap</a>, and it is <i>total</i> on the top-level
--   scope, because the only thing that extends that scope is a definition
--   and every definition is entered here. Bound variables never reach it:
--   <a>showTermWith</a> sends a name back through the binders it passed
--   and only consults the map for what is free in the whole term.
--   
--   It is also the seed of the interner a serialisation layer would need,
--   since a <a>Name</a> is an allocation artefact and cannot be written to
--   disk.
type Display = NameMap

-- | Everything carried from one declaration to the next.
data Env (n :: S)
Env :: Ctx BNFC'Position n -> Table (Name n) -> Table (Name n) -> Map VarIdent (Table (Name n)) -> Display n VarIdent -> Table (Term n) -> Table ([VarIdent], Name n) -> Env (n :: S)

-- | Scope, types and definitions: the foil half.
[envCtx] :: Env (n :: S) -> Ctx BNFC'Position n

-- | Fully qualified names reachable in the module being checked, including
--   what its imports brought in.
[envDeclared] :: Env (n :: S) -> Table (Name n)

-- | Those declarations of the current module that are public.
[envExports] :: Env (n :: S) -> Table (Name n)

-- | What each module checked so far exports.
[envModules] :: Env (n :: S) -> Map VarIdent (Table (Name n))

-- | What each top-level name is called.
[envDisplay] :: Env (n :: S) -> Display n VarIdent

-- | Spellings that stand for a <i>term</i> rather than a name: the
--   manifest fields of the module's parameter block. A manifest field is
--   an abbreviation, so it is never a variable, never discharged over, and
--   resolved by putting its value in place. Emptied at a module boundary,
--   since a parameter block belongs to one module.
[envManifest] :: Env (n :: S) -> Table (Term n)

-- | For each declaration of the module being checked, the parameters it
--   was closed over and its name. A reference to one of them from inside
--   the same module is put back together with those parameters; see
--   <a>splitVisible</a>. It is emptied at a module boundary, since a
--   client sees the closed constant and applies it itself.
--   
--   The declaration's own <a>Name</a> is recorded here, rather than looked
--   up by spelling later, because a module parameter may shadow the
--   spelling. It sits second in the pair so that the pair is a
--   <a>Functor</a> over it, and the whole table sinks as a coercion (see
--   <a>extendEnv</a>).
[envClosedOver] :: Env (n :: S) -> Table ([VarIdent], Name n)

-- | An empty environment, before any module is checked.
emptyEnv :: Env 'VoidS

-- | Extend an environment with one top-level definition.
--   
--   Every map is a container of sinkables, so widening them is a coercion,
--   and only the new entry is inserted. The nested containers (the tables
--   of the module map, the pairs of <a>envClosedOver</a>) are sunk through
--   <a>Compose</a>, the same idiom <a>sink1</a> itself uses one level
--   down, so no spine is walked anywhere.
extendEnv :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => Ctx BNFC'Position l -> NameBinder n l -> VarIdent -> Visibility -> Env n -> Env l

-- | Print a term, showing top-level definitions by name and bound
--   variables by their index.
display :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Env n -> Term n -> RenderedTerm

-- | A name as shown to the user: a fully qualified spelling, not a
--   <a>Name</a>. Distinct from <a>RenderedTerm</a> so that the two cannot
--   be mixed up in a <a>CommandResult</a>.
newtype RenderedName
RenderedName :: String -> RenderedName
[renderedName] :: RenderedName -> String

-- | A term as shown to the user, printed by <a>display</a>. Distinct from
--   <tt>StoredTerm</tt> in <a>Language.MLTT.Artifact</a>, which keeps the
--   term's bytes for loading rather than prose for the user.
newtype RenderedTerm
RenderedTerm :: String -> RenderedTerm
[renderedTerm] :: RenderedTerm -> String

-- | The prose of a failure, whatever layer it came from: a
--   <a>ParseError</a>, a <a>TypeError</a>, or a <tt>LinkError</tt>. By the
--   time it reaches a result, it is only shown.
type ErrorMessage = String

-- | Render a fully qualified name the way results show it.
renderVarIdent :: VarIdent -> RenderedName

-- | What interpreting one declaration produced.
data CommandResult

-- | A module was reached in build order.
EnteredModule :: RenderedName -> CommandResult

-- | A module was loaded from its cached artifact; its <tt>check</tt> and
--   <tt>compute</tt> commands are not re-run.
LoadedModule :: RenderedName -> CommandResult

-- | <tt>def</tt> succeeded, for the fully qualified name and the module
--   parameters it was discharged over.
Defined :: RenderedName -> [RenderedName] -> CommandResult

-- | <tt>check</tt> succeeded, for a term and its type.
Checked :: RenderedTerm -> RenderedTerm -> CommandResult

-- | <tt>compute</tt> succeeded, with the normal form.
Computed :: RenderedTerm -> CommandResult

-- | An interactive <tt>import</tt> brought a module's exports into the
--   session.
Imported :: RenderedName -> CommandResult

-- | The declaration was rejected.
Failed :: ErrorMessage -> CommandResult

-- | Did everything succeed?
succeeded :: [CommandResult] -> Bool

-- | Render a result the way the executable prints it.
renderResult :: CommandResult -> String

-- | What ordering or linking a set of modules can report: a missing or
--   cyclic import, or overlapping reservations.
type BuildError = String

-- | Order the modules so that every module comes after the ones it
--   imports.
--   
--   Reports an import of a module that is not present, and an import
--   cycle, rather than looping or crashing.
buildOrder :: [Module] -> Either BuildError [Module]

-- | The name of a module.
moduleName :: Module -> VarIdent

-- | The parameters of a module.
--   
--   Note that this is the block after <a>resolveUnits</a> has put the
--   included fields in front of it, since that is the only shape a module
--   reaches the checker in.
moduleParams :: Module -> [Param]

-- | The imports of a module.
moduleImports :: Module -> [Import]

-- | The declarations of a module.
moduleDecls :: Module -> [Decl]

-- | The telescopes a program declares, by name.
type Telescopes = Map VarIdent [Param]

-- | Split a program's units and resolve every <tt>include</tt> clause.
--   
--   An include is expanded into the module's parameter block, so that
--   nothing downstream has to know about telescopes: what comes out is an
--   ordinary parametrised module, elaborated and discharged as before.
--   Expanding before the module is hashed is also what makes an include
--   behave like an import for staleness, since a changed telescope changes
--   the printed form of every module that includes it.
--   
--   The included fields come first, in the order the clauses are written,
--   and the module's own parameters follow. A telescope may be included by
--   any number of modules and is elaborated afresh in each, which is what
--   keeps the elaboration canonical: nothing is shared between two modules
--   but the source.
--   
--   A telescope may itself include telescopes, so a theory can extend a
--   poorer theory: <tt>telescope Monoid include Semigroup (unit : A)
--   …</tt> is the monoid block built on the semigroup one. Telescope
--   includes are expanded first, in dependency order over the declared
--   telescopes with a cycle reported by name in the same shape as the
--   build order over modules, so by the time a module includes a
--   telescope, the telescope is a plain parameter list. A refined include
--   composes unchanged, since refining a parameter list yields a parameter
--   list.
resolveUnits :: [Unit] -> Either BuildError [Module]

-- | How many top-level names a module may declare.
stripeSize :: StripeSize

-- | The region module parameters and elaboration-time binders live in:
--   every non-negative name, now that the stripes lie below zero.
--   
--   Nothing here can collide with a declaration's name, and the indices
--   stay small: a discharged type prints as <tt>Π (x0 : 𝕌) → …</tt>
--   however many declarations precede it. More importantly, allocation
--   inside the region depends only on the region's own content, so
--   elaborating a declaration produces the same term whatever else the
--   ambient scope holds. Thus elaborated terms, and hence artifacts and
--   their hashes, are canonical across worlds.
--   
--   What lands here is one name per binder <i>written</i> in the
--   declaration being elaborated, plus the parameters, and the region
--   resets between declarations, since elaboration binders live inside
--   terms and never enter the module's scope. Evaluation and type checking
--   also mint their transient names here (the guarded successor allocates
--   at the region's occupied top), and nothing rests on those.
localRegion :: NameRange

-- | The demo's stripe layout: runs of <a>stripeSize</a> names below zero,
--   descending, per <a>Control.Monad.Foil.Registry</a>. The registry
--   machinery itself lives in the library now; what stays here is this
--   policy.
mlttStripes :: StripeLayout

-- | Which stripe each module's declarations live in; see
--   <a>Control.Monad.Foil.Registry</a> for why the assignment is
--   persistent and append-only. Here it is threaded through one run, and a
--   test (or a driver) can seed it.
type Registry = Registry VarIdent

-- | The registry before any module has ever been checked.
emptyRegistry :: Registry

-- | The stripe of a module, assigning the next one on first use.
--   
--   The demo keeps one flat <a>localRegion</a> rather than a
--   per-declaration <a>RegionLayout</a>: its display shows raw indices
--   directly, and the canonicity of its elaborated terms already holds
--   with the flat region (see <a>localRegion</a>), so it trades the
--   reopening-clash-freedom of regions for small printable names.
registerModule :: VarIdent -> Registry -> (Registry, NameRange)

-- | Where stripe <tt>i</tt> lies, under the demo's layout.
stripeRange :: StripeIndex -> NameRange

-- | Interpret a program: order its modules by their imports, then check
--   each.
interpretProgram :: Program -> [CommandResult]

-- | Interpret units gathered from any number of sources.
--   
--   The telescopes are resolved over all of them at once, exactly as the
--   imports are, so a module may include a telescope declared in another
--   file.
interpretUnits :: [Unit] -> [CommandResult]

-- | Interpret modules whose includes have already been resolved.
--   
--   Build order is computed over all of them at once, so a module may
--   import one declared in another file, or later in the same file.
interpretModules :: [Module] -> [CommandResult]

-- | Check each module in turn, in the growing top-level scope.
--   
--   A module's parameters are elaborated once here, before its
--   declarations, so that a parameter block that does not resolve is
--   reported once rather than against every declaration that would have
--   been checked under it.
goModules :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Registry -> Env n -> [Module] -> [CommandResult]

-- | A module checked on its own: its final environment, at an existential
--   scope index, together with the evidence that everything it added to
--   the scope it started from lies inside its stripe. Two of these over
--   the same start can be linked; see <a>linkModules</a>.
data CheckedModule (c :: S)
[CheckedModule] :: forall (c :: S) (n :: S). DExt c n => ExtWithin c n -> Env n -> [CommandResult] -> CheckedModule c

-- | Open a checked module's existential package.
withCheckedModule :: forall (c :: S) r. CheckedModule c -> (forall (n :: S). DExt c n => ExtWithin c n -> Env n -> [CommandResult] -> r) -> r

-- | The results a checked module reported.
resultsOf :: forall (c :: S). CheckedModule c -> [CommandResult]

-- | Check one module against an environment of already checked modules.
--   
--   Nothing here depends on any sibling: the module sees only what it
--   imports, and its declarations take the names its stripe dictates, so
--   two modules with no import path between them can be checked in either
--   order, or in parallel, and produce identical results.
--   
--   A module's parameters are elaborated once here, before its
--   declarations, so that a parameter block that does not resolve is
--   reported once rather than against every declaration that would have
--   been checked under it.
checkModule :: forall (c :: S). Distinct c => NameRange -> Env c -> Module -> CheckedModule c

-- | Check a module against the environment of an already checked one,
--   composing the evidence, so that a chain of modules, each importing the
--   previous, presents itself as one checked unit over the chain's base.
--   The chain's results accumulate.
--   
--   This is what lets two chains over a shared base be checked in parallel
--   and then linked as wholes: fold each chain with this, then
--   <a>linkModules</a>.
checkModuleAfter :: forall (c :: S). NameRange -> CheckedModule c -> Module -> CheckedModule c

-- | Link two units checked independently against the same environment: two
--   modules, or two chains folded with <a>checkModuleAfter</a>.
--   
--   The two scopes share exactly the names of the common environment, the
--   amalgamated part, identified rather than renamed apart, and extend it
--   only within their reservations, so the whole disjointness obligation
--   is one sweep over two range sets (<a>withDisjointUnion</a>). Each
--   side's tables are then sunk into the union, and the total maps are
--   merged with <a>unionNameMaps</a>.
--   
--   No module registration happens here: each side's <a>envModules</a>
--   already records everything it checked (<a>finishModule</a>), so the
--   union of the two suffices. The result is an environment a further
--   module can be checked in, exactly as if the two sides had been checked
--   in sequence.
linkModules :: forall (c :: S) r. CheckedModule c -> CheckedModule c -> (forall (k :: S). Distinct k => Env k -> r) -> Either BuildError r

-- | Link two units into one, keeping the evidence, so the result links
--   further: a whole build folds through this, wave by wave.
linkChecked :: forall (c :: S). CheckedModule c -> CheckedModule c -> Either BuildError (CheckedModule c)

-- | Merge the environments of two linked units; see <a>linkModules</a> for
--   why nothing but the union is needed.
mergeEnvs :: forall (n :: S) (k :: S) (m :: S). (Ext n k, Ext m k, Distinct k) => ScopeUnion n m k -> Scope k -> Env n -> Env m -> Env k

-- | <a>sink1</a>, with the target index determined by a scope the caller
--   already holds, so that the wanted constraints match the givens of a
--   linking continuation.
sunkTo :: forall f e (n :: S) (l :: S). (Functor f, Sinkable e, DExt n l) => Scope l -> f (e n) -> f (e l)

-- | Record what a module exported, once it is checked.
finishModule :: forall (l :: S). VarIdent -> Env l -> Env l

-- | Exactly two of something.
--   
--   A declaration that elaborates a type and a value, or a term and its
--   type, asks <tt>withElaborated</tt> for both at once. Using this rather
--   than a list is what makes "elaborated the wrong number of terms"
--   unrepresentable instead of an <tt>error</tt> in an unreachable branch.
data Two a
Two :: a -> a -> Two a

-- | Allocate a module's parameters, extending the environment with them.
--   
--   Parameters are allocated in <a>localRegion</a>, below every stripe, so
--   they can never collide with a declaration's name, which is what used
--   to force them to be re-allocated per declaration. They are still
--   elaborated afresh for each declaration, but now only for simplicity: a
--   parameter block is a few small terms, and re-elaborating it keeps
--   <a>withDecls</a> a plain fold.
--   
--   A parameter is nameable by its bare spelling and is not exported,
--   which is exactly what <a>extendEnv</a> does for a private declaration.
--   
--   A <i>manifest</i> parameter binds nothing. Its value is elaborated in
--   the module's own scope, before any of the block's binders, and
--   recorded in <a>envManifest</a>, so the spelling stands for that term
--   wherever it is used. Two things follow, and both are the point of the
--   arrangement. A value cannot mention a bound field of the block, since
--   no such name is in scope where it is elaborated, which is the
--   admissibility condition for a refinement enforced by scoping rather
--   than tested. And nothing is ever discharged over a manifest field,
--   since <a>discharge</a> only ever sees the telescope, which such a
--   field is not in.
withParams :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Env n -> [Param] -> (String -> r) -> (forall (p :: S). DExt n p => ParamTelescope BNFC'Position n p -> Env p -> r) -> r

-- | Elaborate a module's parameter types, reporting the first that fails.
validateParams :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Env n -> [Param] -> Maybe TypeError

-- | Split the visible spellings into a table of names and a table of
--   terms, putting the module's parameters back into references to its own
--   declarations.
--   
--   A declaration is closed at the point it is defined, so a later one in
--   the same module refers to a constant that expects the parameters it
--   was closed over. Rather than making the source apply them, each
--   spelling that reaches such a constant is moved to the terms table of
--   the conversion (<a>tryToTerm'With</a>), where it stands for the
--   constant applied to those parameters. This happens during resolution,
--   so no second pass over the elaborated term is needed.
--   
--   The table of names is consulted first, so a local binder or a
--   parameter shadowing the spelling wins, and nothing can be captured.
--   Outside the declaring module the table of terms is empty, which is
--   right: a client is handed a closed constant and instantiates it as it
--   likes.
splitVisible :: forall (p :: S). Env p -> Table (Name p) -> (Table (Name p), Table (Term p))

-- | Report parameters a declaration needs that it is not being closed
--   over.
--   
--   With the computed set this cannot arise, since that set is closed. It
--   is the answer for a caller that supplies a set of its own.
needsParameters :: [VarIdent] -> TypeError

-- | Report an identifier that did not resolve, with any near spellings.
notInScope :: UnresolvedName VarIdent -> TypeError

-- | Everything a block of declarations is checked in: the module's
--   <a>Block</a> (the stripe its names are allocated from, paired with the
--   linking evidence) and the environment. The scope indices are the
--   module's starting scope <tt>c</tt> and the current scope <tt>n</tt>.
data ModuleEnv (c :: S) (n :: S)
ModuleEnv :: Block c n -> Env n -> ModuleEnv (c :: S) (n :: S)
[moduleBlock] :: ModuleEnv (c :: S) (n :: S) -> Block c n
[moduleEnv] :: ModuleEnv (c :: S) (n :: S) -> Env n

-- | Check a block of declarations at a namespace path.
--   
--   The path is lexical, so a nested <tt>namespace</tt> is just a
--   recursive call with a longer path, and leaving it needs no
--   bookkeeping: the qualified names stay in <a>envDeclared</a> and the
--   bare spellings were never stored, only computed by <a>visibleAt</a>.
--   
--   Every declaration is checked with the module's parameters in scope,
--   and a <tt>def</tt> is then discharged over the ones it uses, so that
--   what is added to the environment lives in the parameter-free scope the
--   module started in.
withDecls :: forall (c :: S) (n :: S) r. Distinct n => ModuleEnv c n -> [Param] -> Path -> [Decl] -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => ModuleEnv c l -> [CommandResult] -> r) -> r

-- | A read–eval–print session: a module that never ends. The session holds
--   a <a>ModuleEnv</a> at an existential scope index, so each step picks
--   up exactly where the previous one stopped, allocating from one
--   interactive stripe.
data Repl (c :: S)
[Repl] :: forall (c :: S) (n :: S). DExt c n => ModuleEnv c n -> Repl c

-- | Start a session over an environment of already checked (or loaded)
--   modules, allocating in the given stripe.
beginRepl :: forall (c :: S). Distinct c => NameRange -> Env c -> Repl c

-- | Feed one input to the session: any run of declarations, including
--   <tt>check</tt> and <tt>compute</tt>.
--   
--   A redefinition allocates a new name and rebinds the spelling,
--   GHCi-style: a term that already refers to the old binding keeps it,
--   since withholding a spelling touches no term.
replStep :: forall (c :: S). SourceText -> Repl c -> (Repl c, [CommandResult])

-- | Parse and interpret one source.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; let report = mapM_ (putStrLn . renderResult) . either error id . interpret
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; report (sourceLines ["module M (A : 𝕌) (x : A)", "def k : A → A := λ y ⇒ y", "def one : A := x"])
--   module M
--     ✓ defined k over (A)
--     ✓ defined one over (A, x)
--   </pre>
--   
--   Each declaration is discharged over the parameters it uses and no
--   others, so what a client sees is a closed definition it applies for
--   itself.
interpret :: SourceText -> Either ParseError [CommandResult]

-- | Parse and interpret several named sources.
--   
--   Each source is parsed on its own, so a syntax error is reported
--   against the line of the file it is in rather than against a
--   concatenation of them all. The units are pooled afterwards, which is
--   what lets one file import a module or include a telescope declared in
--   another.
interpretSources :: [(FilePath, SourceText)] -> Either ParseError [CommandResult]
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Impl.CommandResult
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedName
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedTerm
instance Data.Foldable.Foldable Language.MLTT.Impl.Two
instance GHC.Base.Functor Language.MLTT.Impl.Two
instance GHC.Generics.Generic Language.MLTT.Impl.CommandResult
instance Data.String.IsString Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedName
instance Data.String.IsString Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedTerm
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Language.MLTT.Impl.CommandResult
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedName
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedTerm
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Impl.CommandResult
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedName
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Impl.RenderedTerm
instance Data.Traversable.Traversable Language.MLTT.Impl.Two


-- | Serialisation of checked modules, built from the parts in
--   <a>Control.Monad.Free.Foil.Artifact</a>; what remains here is the
--   artifact record, its envelope, and the driver logic.
--   
--   A raw name of a <i>constant</i> is a registry artefact. The artifact
--   therefore records the constants' qualified spellings, and loading
--   judges them once, at the artifact level (<a>constantRelocation</a>).
--   In the usual case every constant already means here what it meant at
--   check time, and the terms are used exactly as decoded; no term is
--   walked at all. Where the registry moved, one total relocation pass
--   touches the references. A loaded module is an ordinary
--   <a>CheckedModule</a>: it links, and further modules check against it,
--   exactly as if it had just been checked.
--   
--   What makes the cache valid is recorded alongside the terms:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>the name ranges at check time: the actual names of the module's
--   own constants, and of its locals. These are ranges rather than a
--   stripe index, so the artifact does not depend on the loading build's
--   stripe policy. A run whose registry agrees reconstructs the very same
--   raw names, and one whose registry moved the reservation still loads,
--   with the names landing where the new range says. Moreover, the
--   no-overlap assumption the verbatim terms rest on is checked from the
--   recorded ranges, never from the terms;</li>
--   <li>the content hash of each import at check time, so a changed
--   dependency is detected and the artifact rejected rather than linked
--   stale.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   <b>Loading trusts the artifact's terms</b>: nothing is re-checked.
--   This covers the typing, and equally the locals and their scoping. What
--   is judged is the constants' boundary, and it is judged from the
--   spelling table alone, not from the terms. Integrity comes from the
--   hash chain, and the hash is <a>contentHash</a>, a plain FNV-1a over
--   the stored content: collision resistance enough for a build cache, not
--   for an adversary.
--   
--   Terms are stored verbatim (<tt>encodeTerm</tt>). The name layout's
--   sign invariant is what makes the raw ids meaningful: a negative name
--   is an interned constant, resolved by spelling on load, and a
--   non-negative one is a local, canonical by elaboration. Nothing is
--   parsed on load, no spelling ever needs escaping, and the bytes do not
--   depend on what else was in scope at check time. Thus the same module
--   produces an identical artifact, and an identical hash, whatever world
--   it is checked in.
module Language.MLTT.Artifact

-- | A checked module, as written to disk.
data ModuleArtifact
ModuleArtifact :: VarIdent -> StoredLayout -> ContentHash -> [(VarIdent, ContentHash)] -> ContentHash -> Map RawName VarIdent -> [ArtifactDecl] -> ModuleArtifact

-- | The module's qualified name.
[artifactModule] :: ModuleArtifact -> VarIdent

-- | The actual names of the module's own constants and of its locals. Thus
--   the artifact depends neither on the loading build's stripe policy nor
--   on the writer's reservation size, and it loads anywhere its names
--   actually fit; the no-overlap assumption the verbatim terms rest on is
--   a checkable fact of the artifact, and the check is tight.
[artifactLayout] :: ModuleArtifact -> StoredLayout

-- | Of the module's printed source: what an incremental rebuild compares.
[artifactSource] :: ModuleArtifact -> ContentHash

-- | Each import, with its content hash at check time.
[artifactImports] :: ModuleArtifact -> [(VarIdent, ContentHash)]

-- | Over the spellings and declarations below.
[artifactHash] :: ModuleArtifact -> ContentHash

-- | The fully qualified spelling of every constant the stored terms
--   reference. There is one table for the whole artifact, since the
--   module's declarations largely reference the same imports.
[artifactSpellings] :: ModuleArtifact -> Map RawName VarIdent

-- | In declaration (= allocation) order.
[artifactDecls] :: ModuleArtifact -> [ArtifactDecl]

-- | One declaration: everything the environment needs to hold for it.
data ArtifactDecl
ArtifactDecl :: VarIdent -> Visibility -> StoredTerm -> StoredTerm -> ArtifactDecl

-- | Fully qualified.
[adSpelling] :: ArtifactDecl -> VarIdent
[adVisibility] :: ArtifactDecl -> Visibility
[adType] :: ArtifactDecl -> StoredTerm
[adValue] :: ArtifactDecl -> StoredTerm

-- | The 64-bit FNV-1a of some rendered content; see <a>contentHash</a>.
newtype ContentHash
ContentHash :: Integer -> ContentHash

-- | A term as stored: canonical bytes. Equality of stored terms is byte
--   equality, which is what a canonical-artifact property tests.
newtype StoredTerm
StoredTerm :: ByteString -> StoredTerm
[storedBytes] :: StoredTerm -> ByteString

-- | What reading or loading an artifact can report: malformed wire bytes,
--   a stale import hash, or a stored term that no longer resolves.
type ArtifactError = String

-- | Serialise a checked module.
--   
--   The declarations are exactly the names the module allocated in its
--   stripe, in ascending order, which is declaration order; their
--   spellings come from <a>envDisplay</a> and are fully qualified, so the
--   artifact does not depend on what was visible under which shorter
--   spelling at check time.
makeArtifact :: forall (c :: S). VarIdent -> NameRange -> ContentHash -> [(VarIdent, ContentHash)] -> CheckedModule c -> ModuleArtifact

-- | Load a checked module from its artifact, into an environment holding
--   what its imports export: the same starting point <a>checkModule</a>
--   has.
--   
--   The load fails if an import's recorded content hash disagrees with the
--   one supplied, which is how a stale artifact is detected. It does not
--   compare the artifact's stripe with the range supplied: a registry that
--   moved the stripe is the relocation case, and the module simply loads
--   at its new names, consistently with everything else in this run.
loadArtifact :: forall (c :: S). Distinct c => Map VarIdent ContentHash -> NameRange -> Env c -> ModuleArtifact -> Either ArtifactError (CheckedModule c)

-- | Load a module from its artifact into the environment of an already
--   loaded (or checked) unit, composing the evidence: the load-side mirror
--   of <a>checkModuleAfter</a>, so a chain of cached modules folds into
--   one unit over the chain's base and links like anything else.
loadArtifactAfter :: forall (c :: S). Map VarIdent ContentHash -> NameRange -> CheckedModule c -> ModuleArtifact -> Either ArtifactError (CheckedModule c)

-- | Encode an artifact for writing: the envelope, then the derived
--   instances. <a>decodeArtifact</a> is its inverse.
encodeArtifact :: ModuleArtifact -> ByteString

-- | Decode an artifact; reports rather than crashes on anything that is
--   not a current-version artifact. Beyond the envelope, the one shape
--   check the instances cannot express: a spelling-table entry for a
--   non-negative name would spell a non-constant.
decodeArtifact :: ByteString -> Either ArtifactError ModuleArtifact

-- | FNV-1a over a string, 64 bits. A build-cache checksum, not a defence.
contentHash :: String -> ContentHash
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Language.MLTT.Artifact.ArtifactDecl
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Language.MLTT.Artifact.ContentHash
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Language.MLTT.Artifact.ModuleArtifact
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Language.MLTT.Artifact.WireMagic
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Language.MLTT.Artifact.WireVersion
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Artifact.ArtifactDecl
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Artifact.ContentHash
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Artifact.ModuleArtifact
instance GHC.Generics.Generic Language.MLTT.Artifact.ArtifactDecl
instance GHC.Generics.Generic Language.MLTT.Artifact.ContentHash
instance GHC.Generics.Generic Language.MLTT.Artifact.ModuleArtifact
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Artifact.ArtifactDecl
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Artifact.ContentHash
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Artifact.ModuleArtifact


-- | A builder over the module machinery: collect modules, order them by
--   imports, and build them in one of three ways:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><a>Sequential</a>: one module after another in topological order,
--   each absorbed into a growing environment; the classic driver.</li>
--   <li><a>Linked</a>: modules grouped into dependency waves; each wave's
--   modules are checked separately against the same base and then linked
--   as units.</li>
--   <li><a>Parallel</a>: the same waves, with each wave's modules checked
--   on concurrently forked threads.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   All three produce the same results, declaration names included,
--   because names come from the registry's stripes and elaboration is
--   canonical; the spec pins the equality. <a>Sequential</a> is
--   <a>Linked</a> with singleton waves, so one driver serves all three.
--   
--   With a cache directory, each successfully checked module's artifact is
--   written beside the build, and a module whose printed source and
--   imports are unchanged is loaded instead of checked
--   (<a>LoadedModule</a> in the results). Staleness is content-defined, so
--   a rebuilt dependency whose declarations came out unchanged does not
--   dirty its dependants (early cutoff). A cached module's <tt>check</tt>
--   and <tt>compute</tt> commands are not re-run: the cache reconstructs
--   environments, not output.
--   
--   With <tt>--repl</tt>, the build is followed by an interactive session
--   over its result. The session starts seeing nothing, like any module:
--   an <tt>import</tt> brings a built module's exports into scope, or
--   loads a module (and its missing imports) from the cache mid-session.
--   The session allocates from the first stripe the build left free.
module Language.MLTT.Build

-- | How to schedule the checking.
data BuildMode
Sequential :: BuildMode
Linked :: BuildMode
Parallel :: BuildMode

-- | What the command line asked for.
data BuildOptions
BuildOptions :: BuildMode -> Maybe FilePath -> SessionMode -> [FilePath] -> BuildOptions
[optMode] :: BuildOptions -> BuildMode
[optCache] :: BuildOptions -> Maybe FilePath
[optSession] :: BuildOptions -> SessionMode
[optFiles] :: BuildOptions -> [FilePath]

-- | Whether the build is followed by an interactive session
--   (<tt>--repl</tt>).
data SessionMode
BatchOnly :: SessionMode
Interactive :: SessionMode

-- | Build a set of modules.
buildModules :: BuildMode -> Maybe FilePath -> [Module] -> IO (Either BuildError [CommandResult])

-- | <a>buildModules</a>, handing the continuation the environment the
--   build ends in, at its existential scope index, together with the
--   registry, so a session can be started over the result
--   (<a>sessionOver</a>).
buildModulesWith :: BuildMode -> Maybe FilePath -> [Module] -> (forall (c :: S). Distinct c => Registry -> Env c -> [CommandResult] -> IO r) -> IO (Either BuildError r)

-- | Parse several named sources and build them; see <a>buildModules</a>.
buildSources :: BuildMode -> Maybe FilePath -> [(FilePath, SourceText)] -> IO (Either BuildError [CommandResult])

-- | <a>buildSources</a>, handing the continuation the outcome; see
--   <a>buildModulesWith</a>.
buildSourcesWith :: BuildMode -> Maybe FilePath -> [(FilePath, SourceText)] -> (forall (c :: S). Distinct c => Registry -> Env c -> [CommandResult] -> IO r) -> IO (Either BuildError r)

-- | Begin a session over a build. The session is a module that never ends,
--   and like any module it starts seeing nothing: an <tt>import</tt>
--   brings a built module's exports into scope (<a>replImport</a>). Names
--   are allocated from the first stripe the build left free. The registry
--   is append-only, so its size names that stripe.
sessionOver :: forall (c :: S). Distinct c => Registry -> Env c -> Repl c

-- | One interactive <tt>import</tt>.
--   
--   A module the session's world already holds, built before the session
--   or imported earlier, contributes its exports to what the session can
--   name, and nothing else: the import is resolution, exactly as in a
--   module header, except that a later import rebinds a spelling an
--   earlier one brought in, the way a later <tt>def</tt> rebinds one.
--   
--   A module the world does not hold is loaded from the cache: the module
--   and its missing imports, dependency-first, each artifact loaded over
--   the session's current scope at its recorded stripe, so the session's
--   evidence grows by the imports' stripes (<a>composeExtWithin</a>) and
--   the session keeps allocating in its own stripe over the enlarged scope
--   (<a>resumeBlock</a>). Staleness is checked exactly as in the builder:
--   an artifact's recorded import hashes must agree with the artifacts its
--   imports load from.
replImport :: forall (c :: S). Maybe FilePath -> VarIdent -> Repl c -> IO (Repl c, [CommandResult])

-- | The executable's entry point: <tt>mltt
--   [--mode=sequential|linked|parallel] [--cache=DIR] [--repl]
--   [FILES…]</tt>, reading standard input when no files are given.
--   
--   With <tt>--repl</tt>, the files are built first and a session is
--   started over the result; standard input then belongs to the session,
--   so no files means an empty environment rather than a source on
--   standard input. The session is entered even if some declarations
--   failed. The failures were reported, and what did check is there to
--   poke at.
buildMain :: [String] -> IO ()
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Build.BuildMode
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Build.BuildOptions
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.MLTT.Build.SessionMode
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Build.BuildMode
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Build.BuildOptions
instance GHC.Show.Show Language.MLTT.Build.SessionMode
